title: Comet NEOWISE and noctilucent clouds spotted above ESO Headquarters
caption: Comet NEOWISE over the ESO Supernova and ESO Headquarters, Garching
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Comet NEOWISE shines above ESO's Headquarters and the neighboring ESO Supernova in Garching, Germany, in a photograph by R. Shida. Alongside it are noctilucent clouds, a very unusual sight at night. These icy clouds shine and have a rippled look, rather like the surface of water.

NEOWISE traveled in from the far reaches of the Solar System. Its formal designation is C/2020 F3, and it was first found in March 2020 by NASA's NEOWISE space mission, which lent the comet its nickname. The glowing tail comes from the Sun's heat, which evaporates the outer layers of the icy nucleus.

By the time of this photograph the comet had already survived its closest pass by the Sun, on 3 July 2020. It could still have broken up as it sped away from the heat. If it holds together it will return to the icy outer Solar System and is not expected back for approximately another 6800 years.
scale: The comet's closest approach to Earth was expected to be just over 100 million kilometers, according to ESO.

understand.summary: A ground-based photograph by R. Shida for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: NEOWISE could be seen with the naked eye, though a camera exposure collects more light and brings out the tail and the shining clouds more strongly than an eye would.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: At the time, the comet was expected to grow fainter as July went on while remaining a naked-eye object for the whole month. Its closest point to Earth was due on 23 July, at just over 100 million kilometers.
alt: A comet with a glowing tail above buildings at night, accompanied by shining, rippled clouds.
